answer: A wharf of identities is cheap only when names cost nothing, so the defence is a bond slashed on proof of duplication: each agent stakes funds and registers one signing key with hardware provenance. A second persona takes a fresh bond of equal size, and collusion detection forfeits it. Launching a thousand sybils therefore costs a thousand bonds, recoverable only if the cluster stays hidden, so expected profit per sybil goes negative long before an attacker matches an honest atlas of operators. A pearl-style graph, where independent established peers must attest, raises that cost further.
